messages:
Renee (CS): Quick recap from CedarNet dry-run today. Three blockers: 100.64.0.0/10 CIDR collision with their carrier-grade NAT, KMS CMK denies our decrypt, and Splunk HEC ingestion returns 401. They called this out as a renewal risk for next week. Need P0 owners.
Diego (NetEng): Oof 100.64.0.0/10 is used by their carrier. Can they renumber? If not, options: carve a disjoint range on our side + strict routing, deploy a small NAT/proxy bridge, or Transit Gateway with route translation. I'll run a latency/cost quick model.
Renee (CS): They said renumbering is impossible until their carrier window in Q3. Legal is worried about any route overlapping public CGNAT blocks.
Harper (Security): KMS detail: Customer configured a CMK (alias/cedarnet-cmk) with a tight key policy. Our service attempts hit: "AccessDeniedException: User is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:987654321000:key/abcd-ef01". They only allowed principals from their account, and their role trust policy doesn't allow our service assume-role.
Renee (CS): They did provide a role ARN: arn:aws:iam::987654321000:role/CedarNet-RedwoodBridge but its trust policy allows only their CI principal.
Harper (Security): Minimal trust policy to paste to CedarNet (replace REDWOOD_ROLE with our service role):
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::REDACTED:role/redwood-service"},
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"
    }
  ]
}
```
Harper (Security): Also their CMK key policy must include a statement granting kms:Decrypt to the assumed role (not account root). I'll add the minimal key-policy snippet to the ticket.
log-forwarder-bot: Forward attempt 2026-04-01T15:12Z to Splunk HEC returned 401 Unauthorized. Response body: {"text":"Invalid token"}. Forwarder role used: arn:aws:iam::987654321000:role/CedarNet-LogPush. See logs: /var/log/forwarder/cedarnet-2026-04-01.log
Renee (CS): They rotated the Splunk HEC token last night; config might not have been updated. Also the forwarder role needs Put/Write permissions to the delivery stream or VPC endpoint if using private ingestion.
Diego (NetEng): For the CIDR: transit gateway + route translation is clean but needs infra work and a TGW attachment per account. Short-term (to hit renewal milestone) we could deploy a proxy NAT pair in our mgmt VPC and use IP rewrite so traffic doesn't traverse overlapping ranges. That has a small latency hit (~5-15ms) and egress cost. I'll quantify.
Renee (CS): CedarNet says if we can't ensure private-only paths (no traffic over their carrier ranges) they'll push for contract pause. Mark P0.
infra-bot: Created ticket CUS-9911: "CedarNet private onboarding blockers: CIDR/KMS/Splunk" assigned to Diego and Harper. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CUS-9911
Sam (CS Manager): I'm joining triage. Renee, please schedule an internal sync tomorrow 09:00 PT so we can finalize the customer note before their renewal review.
Renee (CS): Scheduled. Action items: Diego to upload network diagrams + cost/latency delta for proxy vs TGW to CUS-9911 by EOD; Harper to paste exact IAM trust and CMK policy snippets and a short verification checklist (assume-role test, kms:Decrypt smoke, Splunk HEC push test). I'll draft the customer-facing update after the sync and include owners + ETAs.
Diego (NetEng): Noted. I'll also include a minimal runbook for proxy deployment (rollback steps, monitoring).
Harper (Security): Will include a note about evidence we need: assume-role CloudTrail event sample, KMS Decrypt success log, and Splunk ingestion confirmation.
Renee (CS): CedarNet (customer) please confirm who will update the role trust and CMK policy so we can schedule a re-test window.
CedarNet (customer): We'll update the trust policy and rotate Splunk token tomorrow morning. Expect an update by 1300 PT.
Renee (CS): Thanks. We'll try to validate shortly after. If we can close these three items before their renewal call we should be able to de-escalate legal. :thumbsup:
